input:
If f(x) = eˣ, g(x) = sin⁻¹x and h(x) = f(g(x)), then h'(x)/h(x) is

Options:
A. e^(sin⁻¹x)
B. 1/√(1-x²)
C. sin⁻¹x
D. e^(sin⁻¹x)/√(1-x²)

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given the composite function h(x) = f(g(x)) where f(x) = eˣ and g(x) = sin⁻¹x, find the ratio h'(x)/h(x).
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: h(x) = e^(sin⁻¹x). The ratio h'(x)/h(x) is the logarithmic derivative of h, i.e., d/dx[ln h(x)] = d/dx(sin⁻¹x) = 1/√(1-x²).

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Write h(x) explicitly as e^(sin⁻¹x), differentiate using chain rule, then divide by h(x) to simplify.
logical_steps: Step 2: Differentiate h(x) using the chain rule

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: h'(x)/h(x) is the logarithmic derivative: d/dx[ln h(x)] = d/dx[sin⁻¹x] = 1/√(1-x²) ✓. The e^(sin⁻¹x) cancels exactly.
